info.name: lpadmin API: full collection
info.description:
Complete API collection for https://lpadmin.blackfx.com (BlackTrader / BlackFX), built from the platform's own sources: the OpenAPI reference (/assets/reference.json), the URI catalogue (GET /v1/uri), the admin and client-site front-end code, and your BlackFX Client Admin collection.

Quick start: import the `lpadmin` environment, fill the email and password variables, run `Admin login` for admin calls and `Trader login` (Trader API, Authentication) for trader calls; both store their token automatically.

Every request says how it was checked. Read-only calls were run live; state-changing calls were not run unless marked. No credentials are stored.

request.description:
**Trader login (email + password) -> session token**

Exchanges a member's email and password for an opaque session token, valid 7 days (memberSessionTTL), to send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

The email is trimmed and lower-cased.

Works for members created in the admin panel and for traders who registered on the client home (both store a bcrypt password hash).

Members auto-created from a foreign userToken (source=iframe) carry a random hash and cannot log in this way.

Failed attempts are throttled per email address.

Source: the platform's official OpenAPI reference (/assets/reference.json).

request.description:
**Exchange an API key for an access token**

Returns a Bearer access token (`oat_…`) valid for one hour; call every trader route with `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` and exchange the key again when it expires.

A token from a `read_only` key is refused on any write (403 "this API key is read-only").

Failed attempts are throttled per key.

`POST /oms/_auth/logout` with the token ends it early.

Source: the platform's official OpenAPI reference (/assets/reference.json).

query.description: Adds symbol, leverage and (when the feed has a spec) min/max/step_volume.
With symbol, include resolved margin_percent, brokerage_rate, markup_rate, brokerage_timing, sell_plain_pnl, valuation_bid_ask and conversion_strict. brokerage already contains mode, min and max.

request.description:
**This account's commercial terms**

The member's resolved account group: live/demo, brokerage, spread markup and IB configuration.

Pass ?symbol= to also get the RESOLVED leverage for that symbol and its volume rules (the numbers the engine gates a fill on).

On an external venue instance (binance, zerodha) this path is intercepted by the venue router and returns the funds shape instead, not these terms.

**On a venue account (binance, zerodha):** returns the funds shape {success, funds, external:true}, not the account-terms object paper returns.

Subgroups inherit nullable scalars and merge rate-table keys.

Per field the precedence is subgroup symbol, subgroup type/default, parent symbol, parent type/default.

With ?symbol=...&terms=resolved, margin_percent, brokerage_rate and markup_rate are resolved by the same engine functions as fills; leverage_pick can only lower the resolved leverage.

Omitting terms=resolved preserves the legacy response shape (including when the effective margin percentage is 100).

M3/M4 add brokerage_timing, sell_plain_pnl, valuation_bid_ask and conversion_strict to the resolved extension. brokerage.mode/min/max plus brokerage_rate give the ticket estimate: max(min(rate × lots, max when positive), min when positive), applying min before max as the engine does.

No commission gate is added.

Source: the platform's official OpenAPI reference (/assets/reference.json).

Checked live on lpadmin 18 Nov 2026: HTTP 200.

Fills immediately at the live feed price (BUY at the ask, SELL at the bid, plus the account group's spread markup), on the account's own leverage and terms.

HEDGING instances (paper, real) open a new position per fill; the response carries `position`.

NETTING instances (paper-net, real-net) apply the ticket to the symbol's single net position and add a `netting` block: action open | add | reduce | close | flip, remaining_qty, and closed_qty/realized_pnl when something closed; `position` is present unless the book went flat.

`reversed` lists the opposite positions a `reverse:true` ticket closed first.

Optional sl/tp attach brackets to the resulting position.

Margin is gated at fill ("insufficient free margin: required …, free …" → 400).

Business refusals on our own books also save a REJECTED order (see EntryRefusal).

Engine refusals are mapped to a status by the wording of the error: messages containing "not found" / "No open position" → 404; "required", "must", "exceed", "unknown symbol", "no live price", "only ", "market closed", "feed stale", "market-data feed", "LIMIT", "STOP" or "empty net position", or a refused lot size → 400; a suspended broker licence → 403 ("trading is suspended for this broker (<reason>) — you can still close positions"); a liquidity-provider (A-book) refusal or absent route → 400 (nothing was placed); an A-book close the LP has no record of → 409 (outcome unknown until the broker checks it); the per-account entry queue being full → 503

**Payout step 2: confirm the code and create the request**

item.name: Request a payout from a funded account

request.description:
**Request a payout from a funded account**

Asks the broker to pay `amount` from a funded prop account to the person's client wallet.

Nothing moves until the broker approves it; the approve checks everything again.

`amount` is at most the payout available (the profit split of the REALIZED balance above the payout base, rounded down to cents), at least the program's `payout_min`, within the free margin, and must not take equity to the account's loss floors.

One open request per account, and a cooldown between payouts (`payout_cooldown_days`, counted from the funded start or the last paid payout).

Idempotent: send an `Idempotency-Key` header or `client_ref`; a retry with the same key and amount answers the first request with 200 and `"replayed": true`.

Source: the platform's official OpenAPI reference (/assets/reference.json).

Not run during checking (state-changing).

request.description:
**Day ranges and new-high/new-low events**

Client supplies its own watchlist symbols; the engine does not own watchlists.

Day maps symbols to actual 1D bucket starts (BLACK/Binance UTC midnight; India configured open, normally 03:45 UTC).

Only seeded breakouts fire.

Default ticks omit exchange time: suppress NH/NL within +/-30s of rollover and reseed.

Compare at shared wire precision: India/Binance >=1 at 4 decimals, BLACK >=1 at 6, below 1 at 8.

Events filter to requested symbols; seq is global.

Reset since if the returned seq decreases after restart.

The ring is not durable replay.

Active-alert interests plus ten-minute API interests are capped at 2000 symbols.

Source: the platform's official OpenAPI reference (/assets/reference.json).
